basis: Brazil audit refreshed after FP3. Visually reviewed FIA Document 15 page 1: the Stewards impose a five-place drop for George Russell's sixth ICE, to be served at his next race, distinguishing the sanction from Technical Delegate Document 14. Document 16 page 1 records Franco Colapinto at 80.6 km/h against the event's 80 km/h pit-lane limit and fines the BWT Alpine F1 Team EUR 100. Document 18 pages 2-3 lists 13 deleted lap-time entries for ten named drivers at turns 1, 7, 10 and 12; these deletions are not a revised finishing classification. Document 19 page 2 orders deletion of the shown FP1 lap times for Franco Colapinto, Alexander Albon, Luke Browning, Rafael Camara and Dino Beganovic after their cars passed through a double-waved-yellow sector; the listed 2:05.129, 1:32.736, 1:33.848, 1:18.760 and OUT LAP entries are lap-time deletions, not a race penalty or revised FP1 classification. Visually checked FIA Document 17 page 2 against the official Formula1.com Practice 1 classification: all 22 entrants and the top three (Norris 1:11.717, Antonelli +0.082s, Verstappen +0.236s) agree. Visually checked new Document 22 page 2 against the official Formula1.com Practice 2 table: the 21 listed timed entrants match, led by Antonelli 1:10.763, Norris +0.253s, Verstappen +0.259s, Russell +0.273s and Piastri +0.321s. Hülkenberg has no timed entry; Formula1.com's report says he did not run. Documents 20 and 21 were visually reviewed: they summon Rafael Camara (Car 51) and Charles Leclerc (Car 16) and their team representatives at 17:40 BRT over an alleged Car 51 impeding Car 16 at Turn 15 at 16:31. The 20:49 UTC listing showed no later ruling at that time; Document 25, published subsequently, resolved the summons with a reprimand. Visually reviewed Document 23 pages 2-3: it lists ten FP2 lap entries for nine drivers (Albon appears twice) after track-use issues at Turns 1 and 4 and orders the listed lap times deleted, not a race penalty or a revised classification. Visually reviewed Document 24 page 1: it requires staying below 1:13.0 between the Safety Car lines during and after Qualifying and on reconnaissance laps while pit exit is open for the Race. Document 13 entry list page 2 confirms 22 race entrants and six additional FP1 stand-ins. Document 10 records a Mercedes curfew exception with no action; Document 9 records timely self-scrutineering submissions and Câmara's cockpit exit/driver-knee clearance. Existing reviews of Documents 8, 12 and 14 remain in force; Document 12's McLaren four-item declaration and ten nil returns, including its page-3 component diagram, were previously reviewed. Upgrade aims are not measured gains. Visually reviewed newly published FIA Document 25 pages 1-2 using the revision-bound screenshots for PDF SHA-256 7c471fd8eac915b0c513152084dcacbf17606bd4eaac9dae091f09e900a4a28f: Camara was reprimanded for unnecessarily impeding Leclerc in FP2; this resolves the summons and does not change the classification or impose a grid drop. Visually reviewed FIA Document 26 pages 1-4: its Technical Delegate report records technical checks before, during and after FP1/FP2; it notes FP2 weighing of car 55, rear-brake pressure-control checks on cars 63, 12, 16, 44, 30 and 43, and fuel/oil sampling of cars 43 and 23. The report states all listed items complied with the 2026 Technical Regulations; sampled fuel/oil matched approved references and fuel-density changes were within limits. Newly reviewed FIA Document 28, Power Unit Information V2, page 2 (PDF SHA-256 ac646baaf86f1a4cd8a8825f7dbdc9afa910967666b52c825a1f1f4087547750) against its prior issue: the revised sheet removes TBC from Overtake detection (3250 m, timing loop L17), confirms activation at 3411 m/L18, and adds a 240 km/h higher-speed threshold at T11 over 2870–2970 m. The existing recharge, power-limited distance/rate, sector windows and reduction/reset limits were visually checked against the new page. FIA Document 27, Curfew, page 1 (PDF SHA-256 e21e3cdf9a8eb3de512f521f9d4257defd170bc1a5028de0b6e61af806f1a183) reports Red Bull and Aston Martin personnel inside the pre-FP3 curfew, their second and third of four permitted exceptions, respectively; the report says no action should be taken. Visually reviewed FIA Document 30 pages 2–3 (PDF SHA-256 46cf930a47e6c2c00c72268450a6c273bde80272c374620795f70d132c623f44): the new-element table lists Verstappen’s fifth ICE, TC and EXH (four allowed), sixth PU-ANC (six allowed); Leclerc and Hamilton’s fifth ICEs; Perez’s fifth ICE/TC, fourth MGU-K and fifth PU-ANC; Russell’s sixth PU-ANC. Visually reviewed Document 31 page 1 (SHA-256 e3a5c05fad1363db54cacad709941dc72908e0a6522b9afc911b2eb01208e572): it is the summons for Perez (Car 11) over the alleged unsafe condition of Car 3 at 12:22 BRT, with a 13:00 BRT hearing; the 16:05 UTC listing still showed the summons and no corresponding ruling. Document 32 page 2 (SHA-256 6e43359e6064ad1ea0d5f9f614992a8105a26d6d79c0c4a8364cc229b110205f) matches the official Formula1.com FP3 classification. Visually reviewed newly published Document 33 page 1 (SHA-256 bd691401ff5f907ceccd81f1169d4eda09669697f5abe64ee6aeb46ce17342db): the Stewards impose a 30-place drop on Max Verstappen for the fifth ICE, TC and EXH for the next Race; if Car 3 is classified in Qualifying, its Race grid position is allocated under Article B2.5.4.b.iv. This is separate from the earlier Formula1.com “back of grid” report. The first direct request for Document 29 returned HTTP 403; the normal FIA media refresh later retrieved it at 16:31:08 UTC. Visually reviewed PDF pages 2–4 (SHA-256 df3c526b9d1ca2ac698fe4cfaff63a73ba8be79597e0d0a8be692f9630173dfb): page 2 sets the top-three post-Q3 return, FIA weighing in race gear, Parc Fermé interviews, and media-access rules; it also specifies weighing and interview duties for other qualifying drivers. Page 4 contains the Parc Fermé diagram. The verified procedure is now summarized on Brazil's Schedule page. Visually reviewed all substantive pages (PDF pages 2–8) of the newly published FIA Race Director’s Competition Notes V2, dated 7 November (SHA-256 74845b23b57e43bc61fc7110d0d955fcfe4b6d9333c2ef7beba3df2870c1fc34). The magenta changes on page 5 require cars not performing practice starts to leave the Pit Exit Road at the earliest opportunity, join the normal line and not cross back into the exit road; page 6 limits crossing the separating white line on Race reconnaissance laps to cars leaving the pit lane without a practice start, and prohibits overtaking on the Pit Exit Road during Qualifying unless a car slows with an obvious problem. The other substantive pages were visually checked for revised competition procedures, safety-car placement, collective test items and circuit changes; no other magenta amendments were found. Added the verified V2 source and page references to Brazil’s Circuit Guide. The previously reviewed 1:13.0 Safety Car-line limit remains sourced to separate FIA Document 24. Visually reviewed new FIA Documents 35 and 37, page 1: Document 35 imposes a 10-place drop for Charles Leclerc's fifth ICE; Document 37 imposes a 10-place drop for Lewis Hamilton's fifth ICE, each for the next Race in which the driver participates. Document 36 page 2 lists Rafael Camara's 1:34.799 at 11:35:37 (Turn 1) and Max Verstappen's 1:52.648 at 11:57:43 (Turn 4), and orders those lap times deleted; this is not itself a revised FP3 classification. Visually reviewed FIA Document 38 page 1: due to anticipated severe weather, all teams are allowed to close their garage doors; the note announces no session delay. These documents were reviewed against their source-bound screenshots. Document 29 was subsequently recovered by the normal FIA media refresh; its substantive pages were visually reviewed and remain hash-bound above. Visually reviewed the newly published FIA Document 39 page 1 (PDF SHA-256 a0aeb23765c2a4a371931feaadd7d02aca38811262b1f09b31ed180c25d575f7): Sergio Perez (Car 11) used a fifth ICE, fifth turbocharger and fourth MGU-K in FP3; the Stewards imposed a 30-place drop for the next Race. If Car 11 is classified in Qualifying, its Race-grid position is allocated under Article B2.5.4.b.iv. This is separate from Document 30, whose fifth PU-ANC for Perez is within the six-part allowance. Visually reviewed all substantive pages (PDF pages 1-2) of FIA Document 40 (PDF SHA-256 2092a003604f54443c592893a003303a68f6b188e696900bab7674e834e713c7), which resolves Document 31: after reviewing in-car video, the Stewards found Perez threw a small plastic cable organiser that had detached from his seat belt out of the car during FP3. Cadillac received a formal warning because throwing material onto the track during a live session was inappropriate; the decision notes the item was small and unlikely to cause damage or injury. The warning is distinct from the power-unit grid penalty.
